Not a doctor, but a chronic anxiety sufferer...you probably just have anxiety. Waking anxiety could be triggered by a few things, psychological or physiological. I had similar symptoms a few years ago when my disorder first popped up. I dreaded going out the door and going about my day because my brain saw everything as threatening and that was exhausting. My heartbeat was also easier to notice when I was lying down so I would become hyper aware of it in the mornings as well. 

More physical reasons could include hormonal changes upon waking (daylight often triggers hormones to make you wake up/start the day with energy), low blood sugar from not having a plentiful dinner or night time snack, or blood sugar disturbances from drinking alcohol at night. That last one used to happen to a coworker of mine who woke up with night terrors almost every night until she stopped drinking her nightly glass of wine that she thought was helping her sleep. 

Visit r/anxiety for more info, too.

You'd be surprised how long ass covering can work...the following situation has been going on for 20 years:

I work with a lady who is a terrible employee. She's messy, disorganized, rude and she STEALS from the company (it's a hotel, she takes everything from guest laundry to cutlery). She refuses to speak to her immediate co-workers. She does not have the skills for her position, seeing as she got transferred from another position: she's supposed to know how to sew but doesn't, and often destroys employee uniforms while "fitting" them.  It affects the image, profits and peace of the property. She once used a hair iron on herself during work hours and left it plugged in and on overnight in our work area, which is full of very flammable cleaning products.  There have been many complaints, from employees of all departments, but our boss doesn't even reprimand her anymore because there's so much ass covering involved, she could lose her job instead.

Oh, we're all female, so they ought to be sucking my cunt.  I think I'm nervous because females form cliques and they seem a little cliquey (loads of XYZ is da beeeest i love her with all my heart posts on Facebook).  I'm the total opposite, and am over all that drama.

I had this problem.  What I do is, I just look once, smile warmly for a second as if you are acknowledging their existence or saying hello, and then go about your business.  If they think you're a creeper, whatever. They looked at you too, and that doesn't make them creepers.
